subject: Distance3.5 and Distance7.3 giving different population density estimates

messages.author: f1437126fe4decd6
messages.subject: Distance3.5 and Distance7.3 giving different population density estimates
parts:
Hi

 

I am fairly new to the application of Distance Sampling.

 

We use Distance Sampling to estimate population densities as a trend over time.

 

Up until last year we were still able to use Distance 3.5.  However, due to operating system upgrades we now have to keep up with the times and use Distance7.3.

 

Using last year’s data I do not seem to be able to replicate the same or similar density estimates using 7.3 as were calculated using 3.5.

 

Without going into the specific details at this stage I am wondering whether you have any initial thoughts on how to rectify this.

 

Robbie

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Distance3.5 and Distance7.3 giving different population density estimates
parts:
Good morning Robbie.

It is impressive that you've been using Distance 3.5; I note that it was released in late 1998; more than 20 years ago.  There have been extensive enhancements both to the theory of distance sampling and software during that period.  In the Distance Users Guide, the list of software revisions between versions 3.5 and 7.3 runs to seven pages.

Could you provide me with output for last year's data from the two software versions off-list?  I'll investigate the nature of the differences (point estimates, measures of precision, etc.) and we can discuss.
